about: Cargo 1's named locations and the real star systems their codes stand for. Astronomy as published by November 2026; colonies, industry and politics are invented. 'rename' is a proposed change to the name the game shows.

Alpha.facts: Proxima b, an Earth-mass planet in Proxima's habitable zone. A Saturn-mass candidate (S1) imaged once by JWST in Alpha Cen A's habitable zone in August 2024, not seen in 2025; unconfirmed.
Alpha.colony: The oldest colonies (Proxima, 2223 in the wiki). Stable, crowded, expensive. Every customs rule in the near systems was written here first.

Beta.facts: Four small planets (0.2 to 0.3 Earth masses), all closer in than the habitable zone.
Beta.colony: Agricultural, as in the wiki, but no planet is cool enough: the farms are rotating drums lit by mirrors. Booming. The agrobots here are Sowers.

Gamma.facts: A flare star; no planets known.
Gamma.colony: Free Colonies mining (wiki). Declining: the good rock is gone and the flares cook the equipment. The miners are the first to strike.

Delta.facts: Planets b and c, each about one Earth mass, in the habitable zone; a third planet d (2024).
Delta.colony: The young colony on c. Formative: everything is on order.

Epsilon.facts: A Jupiter-mass planet at 3.5 AU on a near-circular orbit; an inner warm disk and an outer belt at about 70 AU.
Epsilon.colony: Stations on the giant's moons; the near systems' ore exchange. Stable.

Omega XIV.facts: A debris disk far heavier than the Sun's Kuiper belt; its planets e and f are no longer thought habitable.
Omega XIV.colony: The wiki's Synthesis habitats: humans and machines sharing one payroll.

Sigma VII.facts: A cold giant planet (Ab) imaged directly by JWST in 2024; a pair of brown dwarfs (Ba, Bb) far out.
Sigma VII.colony: Ice mining on the giant's moons. Declining.

Theta III.facts: A bright debris ring where planetesimals collide: Hubble saw one collision cloud in 2004 and a second in 2023.
Theta III.colony: Salvage of a belt that keeps smashing itself. Booming.

DSO-Alpha.facts: The nearest pair of brown dwarfs.

DSO-Beta.facts: The coldest known brown dwarf, about 265 K; JWST saw its water clouds thicken and thin as it turns (2026).

DSO-Gamma.facts: A red dwarf and a brown dwarf that passed through the Sun's outer Oort cloud, about 0.8 ly out, some 70,000 years ago.
DSO-Gamma.colony: A quiet outpost. In the story the star took a piece of the Gyrotron with it on the way past.

Nova Labs.facts: A flare star with planet candidates, none confirmed.
Nova Labs.colony: Research colonies, as in the wiki. Stable.

Quantum Center.facts: Three small planets on tight orbits; radio bursts thought to come from the innermost planet stirring the star's magnetic field.

Stellar Institute.facts: Seven rocky planets, several in the habitable zone.
Stellar Institute.colony: The far research station. Formative. Matylda Korinek works here.

Ancient Ruins Alpha.facts: The clustered orbits of the most distant known Kuiper belt objects (the wiki's Solar System Hypothesis).
Ancient Ruins Alpha.colony: None. Segments of a broken ring, in our own outer system.

Ancient Ruins Beta.colony: The segment Scholz's Star pulled away. It still turns.

Alien Outpost X.colony: Automated, empty. No aliens: the trilogy only hints at them.

Alien Outpost Y.colony: A beacon pointing outward, at nothing anyone can see yet.

Zeta.facts: A pair of Sun-like stars; Zeta-2 has a debris disk. Famous in Earth's flying-saucer stories.
Zeta.colony: Capital of the Cult of the Broken Machine.

Eta.facts: Warm dust that looks like the aftermath of a comet bombardment.
Eta.colony: Comet catchers. Prices go wild after every impact.

Theta.facts: A red dwarf in a triple system with at least one planet in its habitable zone.

Omega-1.facts: A wide, smooth disk with no obvious planets carving it.
Omega-1.colony: A base in a disk nobody can explain.

DSO-Delta.facts: Long thought one brown dwarf; resolved into a tight pair in 2024.
DSO-Delta.colony: The outpost's sign was repainted when the dwarf turned out to be two.
